Some days I can tolerate Isgarren's mental games, and others... I. Can. Not. Ever since Sorrow's sudden departure, my patience with him has lessened. I can't help but think that he pushed her away from us, but... I must remind myself to breathe. Lyhr's presence has been a boon on this front. He is always there to cool my ever-boiling blood. After all, I am now a leader of this...place. I need to—per Lyhr's encouragement—"behave."  
  
Some of the newer recruits are unsettled by our appearances. Lyhr usually gets a delighted response, given that he isn't made of stone, but Isgarren, Mabon, and I are usually met with fear. Mabon chose to hide his wings to lessen the dire presence of a mursaat, and Isgarren has taken on a blue complexion, hoping that he may be mistaken for a djinn, but I... Why is it that the presence of a jotun—and a woman at that—is so shocking? I realize that my people are different now than they were when I was rescued those many years ago, but... For Isgarren to ask me to hide myself? To change myself? No. I could've killed him on the spot, but I knew I'd be dead before the thought finished. Or worse.  
  
Days like today make me want to drop everything and find her. Waiting Sorrow. I...should be angry, but she was always a warm voice in the swirling, terrifying expanse of the cosmos. I realize that she broke about every rule in the book by leaving with her powers intact, but I will always wonder why...  
  
I will always miss her.

Wayfinder!

My mind is still...reeling from the ordeal, but with your help and Mabon's, I'm on the right path again. Flickering images still cross my mind. Faces... A name.

Enough of that. I'm writing because I wanted to give you something. Before she left, Waiting Sorrow gave me this to me. Dagda told me that you were helping her rebuild the Oracle Deck, so this should put you one step closer.

Cheers,
Lyhr

I don't recognize this place. Not anymore.

The Nahpui Quarter was my home, once... Now it smells like rotting flesh, piled high in the hull of a ship. It stood long enough for us to escape. Now it's filled with our...dead. Our families. Our people. Walking like they still live, and yet... I hope we're not facing another Affliction.

The rebuilding of Kaineng will start just to the south of here; a land filled with naga and a thousand other beasts. We'll work our way down from there, gutting the old swamp until it resembles something livable. That's the plan, at least.

An old recycling facility remains on the border of Old Kaineng ("Old" being a peculiar word to write or say aloud). Once we've cleared it of the "Risen," Officer Jimin wants to use it to build weapons.

Researcher Doh Taelin, Ministry of Archives, 1729 CC
